messages:
Diego (sales): ACME POC update: their QA team says our private hostname resolves only from their management subnets, but the app nodes return NXDOMAIN. Can we triage DNS split-horizon / private zone issues? :mag:

ACME-Networking: Confirmed. Management subnets (10.1.0.0/24) can resolve private.redwood-acme.internal -> 10.2.3.4. App subnets (10.1.10.0/24) get NXDOMAIN. We didn't change route tables recently. Here's dig from a failing app node:

ACME-Networking: ```dig @10.0.0.2 private.redwood-acme.internal +short

;; -> no output (NXDOMAIN)
```

Priya (solutions): Two likely causes: 1) private hosted zone not associated with the app VPC, or 2) there is a custom resolver rule or firewall between VPCs. Can you paste `resolv.conf` or the VPC association list?

ACME-Networking: resolv.conf from app node:

ACME-Networking: ```nameserver 10.0.0.2
options ndots:5
```

ACME-Networking: And route53 associations: hosted zone "private.redwood-acme.internal" associated with VPC vpc-aaa (management) but not vpc-bbb (app). We thought shared resolver rules would cover it.

Liam (neteng): If the private hosted zone isn't associated with the app VPC, the resolver will return NXDOMAIN for the app VPC. Shared resolver rules only forward queries to the right place; they don't magically attach private zone records to another VPC. You can either associate the hosted zone with the app VPC or create an outbound/inbound resolver endpoint + rule.

Jia (eng-runtime): For a fast POC workaround: we can add a short-lived CNAME in the app VPC (if they allow us) pointing to the existing record, or provide a fallback public hostname that resolves to the same IP over the private path. We can also add an IP-based host entry on the app instances as a last resort for demos. Which is acceptable?

ACME-Networking: Security says we cannot add host entries at scale. They prefer not to change hosted zone associations without review. Inbound resolver endpoints require security review too. Any option that avoids changing VPC associations?

Priya (solutions): Another path: we can spin up an interface VPC endpoint (AWS Route53 resolver inbound endpoint) in their app VPC that forwards queries to the VPC holding the private zone; but that needs security approval for ENIs. For immediate unblock: we can expose a dedicated POC IP (NAT/ALB) in the management VPC and ask you to add a route from app VPC -> transit gateway to that IP. That avoids touching DNS for the short demo window. It's similar to previous POC pattern.

ACME-Networking: We'd prefer to avoid new routes. Could you instead give a different hostname we can add to their internal allowlist that resolves publicly but only reachable from their VPC via a peered interface? How would that work?

Jia (eng-runtime): We can provision `poc-public-redirect.acme.redwood.internal` as a public DNS name that resolves to an ALB IP controlled by us. Then we apply a security group + IP whitelist so only ACME VPC traffic can reach it. The DNS is public, but the endpoint is protected. That requires adding a single outbound permission on their firewall to reach that IP (less invasive).

Liam (neteng): From network POV that's much easier: only need to allow outbound to 198.51.100.45/32 during the demo window. No change to Route53 associations. ACME, can you add that egress rule for a 48-hour window?

ACME-Networking: Potentially yes, but Security wants to see the public IP and a formal rollback date. Also we need to know if this will require cert changes (SNI) or if TLS will still present the private hostname cert.

Jia (eng-runtime): We'll terminate TLS at the ALB using a cert that has both `private.redwood-acme.internal` and `poc-public-redirect.acme.redwood.internal` in SANs. So no client changes on their side; apps still call the private hostname if we give them a local override, or they can call the public hostname we provide. Cert rotation for POC: short-lived cert, no change to production certs.

Diego (sales): Pricing/POC scope Q from ACME: will spinning up a dedicated ALB + public IP for the 48-hour test add to their bill or our POC commitment? They asked whether this is included.

Priya (solutions): For POC we absorb infra costs for up to 72 hours demos. If they need longer-term changes (hosted zone associations, inbound endpoints) we'll discuss enterprise private onboarding fees. For now this is on us.

ACME-Networking: OK please share the IP and exact time window we need to allow. Also we need a short security note on why hosted zone association isn't being changed yet and a rollback plan.

Jia (eng-runtime): Deploy plan: create ALB + target group, attach cert with SANs, IP 198.51.100.45 assigned. TTL=60s. We'll stand it up in ~25 mins. Rollback: ALB removed and IP released after 48 hours; cert revoked/removed.

deploy-bot: Task queued: create-poc-alb(198.51.100.45) -> status: queued

Liam (neteng): ACME, please confirm the earliest window you can open egress for 198.51.100.45 and who signs off. We'll wait on sign-off before flipping DNS/fallback.

Diego (sales): I'll coordinate sign-off with ACME security and circle back here. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

ACME-Networking: Thx team, we'll reply with the approval time and contact. If this works we can document the long-term fix (hosted zone association + resolver endpoint) for the later rollout.
